teaser.en: Each clove is a flower bud picked before it could open, dried and shipped from the islands of Zanzibar and Pemba.

summary.en: *Karafuu* is the clove, the dried flower bud of a tropical tree, imported from Zanzibar and Pemba. It spices pilau, tea and coffee.

about.en: Cloves are the dried, unopened flower buds of an evergreen tree in the myrtle family. Each looks like a small brown nail, with a round head and a slender stem, and has a strong, warm, pungent scent.

where.en: Cloves are not grown on the south coast; they are imported from Zanzibar and Pemba and sold in markets.

uses.en: Cloves spice pilau, tea and coffee.

names.en: The Digo name is *karafuu*, the same as in Swahili. In English it is clove.

reason.en: Coffee, which cloves help to spice

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
